fact: ITWeb Africa reports that the Electronic Government (Amendment) Bill, revising the Electronic Government Act No. 41 of 2021, was presented at a SMART Zambia Institute stakeholder meeting in January 2026 (a bill, not in force); the article describes its content as legal standing for electronic submissions and digital authentication, and ties it to moving from independent digital systems to an integrated ecosystem and to the vendor-locked systems that prevent data sharing, but does not say the bill itself provides for public bodies exchanging data; the date is the article's published date.
source_slug: 2026-01-23 Zambia begins amending Electronic Government Act

fact: The Electronic Government Act, 2021 (Act No. 41 of 2021, an act of Parliament, assented 19 May 2021) is an enacted e-government law whose own text provides for public bodies sharing data: s.12(3) lets a public body retrieve documents from the issuing public body with the data subject's consent, and s.17 provides for joint automated procedures between public bodies.

The Electronic Government Act, 2021 (Act No. 41 of 2021) only permits sharing between public bodies: s.12(3) says a public body 'may' retrieve documents from another public body with consent, and s.17(1) says it 'may' implement joint automated procedures; neither obliges exchange or connection, and no regulation made under it is mentioned.
